knowledge_gaps: Low one-draw competitor coverage can be expected even under correct uniform sampling. For m draws with replacement from M eligible negatives, each competitor has inclusion probability 1−(1−1/M)^m. The audit needs sampler-specific expected coverage, repeated draws, and uncertainty before interpreting low coverage as a training weakness.

Fresh negatives sampled after training measure current sampler coverage, not which competitors the optimizer encountered during training. These claims must remain separate unless actual training exposure was logged.

The motivating margin and catalog-HR measurements use different training examples and aggregation schemes. Measure both on identical prefix–target pairs before attributing their discrepancy to negative sampling.

Captured softmax mass includes the target in its denominator, so changes can reflect target confidence as well as negative coverage. Report target probability and negative-conditional captured mass separately. Temperature 1 fixes the calculation but does not make scores calibrated or comparable across category models.

Paired coverage differences become undefined when either variant has no strict outrankers. Specify complete-pair aggregation, report zero-outranker transitions separately, and quantify selection caused by failed replacement matching.

Reproduction still requires concrete negative draw counts, sampling exclusions, replacement repetitions, bootstrap counts, scoring precision, runtime caps, and a four-category aggregation mechanism outside the single-ModelView probe.

Originality 5 is plausible for integration, but potential 8 lacks evidence that this audit guides validation gains. Difficulty 3 appears optimistic given sampler fidelity and paired uncertainty. A simpler clean-prefix audit should precede the replacement extension; any later loss experiment needs matched sampling and compute controls.

follow_up_queries.reason: Establish a sampling baseline so mechanically low coverage is not mistaken for inadequate optimization, and distinguish fresh diagnostic sampling from cumulative training exposure.
follow_up_queries.query: For sequential recommenders trained with sampled negatives, how should coverage of exact catalog target-outranking items be normalized by expected inclusion probabilities under uniform, popularity-weighted, and rejection sampling? Include repeated-draw uncertainty, sampling with versus without replacement, and the distinction between post-training sampler coverage and cumulative optimizer exposure.

follow_up_queries.reason: Clarify whether coverage and captured score mass diagnose the actual training objective sufficiently to justify an optimization change.
follow_up_queries.query: In next-item recommendation with a frozen NextItNet and sampled-negative training, what evidence connects negative-set competitor coverage or captured catalog softmax mass to gradient quality and held-out ranking? Compare binary cross-entropy, BPR, and sampled-softmax objectives, including duplicate multiplicity, target-inclusive versus negative-conditional mass, score-scale sensitivity, and false negatives.

follow_up_queries.reason: Resolve paired-estimator and selection issues before extending the existing replacement probes.
follow_up_queries.query: For paired recommender history-replacement diagnostics with fixed candidate catalogs, how should user-cluster uncertainty be estimated when outranker coverage is undefined for zero-outranker cases and replacement matching fails for some prefixes? Discuss common-support paired estimands, zero-outranker transitions, nested negative-sampling Monte Carlo error, and selection bias from complete-case analysis.
